summary: Feed s138_double is degraded for APM: 50% of packets missing required VLAN 20 (untagged) and 63.8% remain ERSPAN-encapsulated, preventing correct VLAN-aware correlation and L7 decoding.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 is not arriving tagged - 50% of packets are untagged. Most likely the ingress SPAN/TAP trunk is not forwarding VLAN 20 or the packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags on ingress/egress instead of preserving them.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires VLANs 10 and 20 for segmentation. Traffic from VLAN 20 is invisible or misclassified, breaking service maps, per-VLAN latency/SLA calculations and filtering for that tenant/segment.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 through the broker to the APM so it can correctly classify and monitor both segments.

findings.root_cause: 63.8% of frames (1305/2047) arrive inside ERSPAN encapsulation. Broker is forwarding ERSPAN from the source without terminating/decapsulating before delivery to the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees outer ERSPAN headers instead of inner application traffic. It cannot parse inner L3-L7 headers, so transaction decoding, flow correlation and latency measurements fail and tool cycles are wasted on tunnel overhead.

recommended_fix.why: Terminate ERSPAN at the packet broker and deliver only the inner native frames so APM can decode applications and measure performance correctly.
